svg.text: Plan: built and planned, north up
above (drawn by an edge's deepest layer)
a way that opens from one side first
The village on the valley road

path.title: a bricked bay; opens from castle.well-head
a steel door barred on the inside; opens from lake.intake-tower
a barrow wedged in the gap of the rubble infill; opens from castle.lower-ward

circle.title: castle.road: Two unequal towers frame a wedge of sky; only the great hall roof shows over the first curtain.
castle.gatehouse: The defended gate. The guardroom opens to one side; the lower ward is ahead.
castle.lower-ward: A working ward under the switchback to the upper court.
castle.upper-ward: The keep shows a second time, the armillary above its south gable. Hall, wall walk and kitchen all leave from here.
castle.hall: The raised end of the hall with its hearth and the gallery above.
castle.kitchen: The kitchen, with the open well of the service stair going down.
castle.cellar: Barrel racks under a low vault; lime lines on the masonry mark an old damp level.
castle.cellar-door: Past a blind bay, an iron-strapped door hanging ajar. Cold air and a thin mineral streak.
forest.trailhead: Bracken in the light, staggered trunks hiding the next bend, far crowns merging into a ridge.
forest.fallen-tree: The windthrow where both trails cross: an open root plate, and one glimpse of the broken bell gable.
forest.nave: The old nave floor below the forest soil, past three root vaults and the bell gable.
forest.cloister: A gap in the canopy lights the flooded garth; ferns in the joints of the low arcade.
forest.crypt: Stairs past half-buried windows to the crypt, and a root-split opening behind it.
crater.notch: From the notch between two hills: a broken ring of mountains with one missing tooth, and the hole at the bottom of the funnel.
crater.lip: Split basalt blades frame the open shaft; the shelf goes under the lip and comes back into sight across it.
crater.throat: The bottom of the spiral. Looking up, a narrowing oval of sky.
under.squeeze: Rock within arm's reach on both sides; the chamber is framed ahead while still standing in the seam.
under.west-shelf: Open air under a tall vault: the bridge ahead, the river below through gaps, the calcite curtain to the left.
under.bridge-crown: The middle of the natural bridge: both river circuits visible below, a distant wall on either hand.
under.east-shelf: The eastern end of the bridge; ramps drop north and south onto the riverbed.
under.river-fork: A low stone bar across the river under the bridge; the fault gallery opens to the north.
under.fault-landing: Fractured rock opens onto the riverbed, the bridge overhead and a cold reflection below.
under.south-bar: The river's last pool in the chamber, before it enters a seam in the south wall.
forest.north-bend: The east trail's furthest point north; the wood goes on, older, toward the crater.
lake.gut: Ankle-deep in the river with a hand on each wall. The noise of the fall arrives before any light.
lake.falls-head: The river drops 28 m past the right shoulder and the whole lake is below; far off, a dead lamp on a tower in the water.
lake.falls-foot: Spray and noise; shingle leading away both ways under the wall.
lake.west-landing: A masonry quay with mooring rings and the ribs of a boat.
lake.well-foot: The bottom of a shaft 13 m across; 66 m up, a disc of lantern light.
castle.well-head: Behind the cellar's blind bay: an arcade round a shaft, and a ramp winding down behind it.
lake.east-shallows: A pale gravel bar where the root chute ends; no way back up it.
lake.intake-tower: A concrete tower standing in the lake to the cavern roof, a gallery at the waterline, a stair up and a stair down.
lake.outflow: A low arch where the lake leaves, east.
deep.gallery: A tunnel under the lake bed, thick glass ports in its roof and the water above them.
deep.sluice: Wheels and a wall of glass: the lake from below, and the white of the fall through 80 m of water.
deep.south-pipe: A pipe 3 m across running south.
village.west-gate: Two leaning posts and a pinfold; the high street bends out of sight.
village.green: A dry well, a market cross and doors left open; lanes go up to the chapel and down to the water.
village.chapel: The widest view on the south side: the castle, the wood and the crater's shoulder in one sweep.
village.ford: A mill wheel, stepping stones, and beside them one flat-roofed building that is plainly not the village's.
village.pump-house: Tiled walls, a rusted lift cage, a stair in a shaft 6 m square; the fall can be heard through the grille.
saddle.beacon: The stump of a round tower, half its wall fallen outward down the slope.
saddle.beacon-top: The armillary to the south, the crater's far headwall filling the north.
saddle.postern-road: Cart ruts through surviving setts, below the castle's blocked west arch.
crater.west-shoulder: The highest walkable point: the armillary, the gate towers, the beacon and the chapel all in view, the throat below.
crater.east-breach: The low remnant of the east rim where the wood meets the apron; the split blades 56 m off.

svg.text: Split basalt blades at the throat
Far headwall with the missing tooth
The west spire of the rim
